text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- A Tallinn meeting of the Baltic prime ministers failed to produce a joint written declaration attesting readiness to start negotiations to join the EU but only an oral one. Differences lay in Baltic views of the attitude of EU countries to the three countries.
- Parliament passed a customs law, seen as a compromise between the transit business and the state revenue service. Latvian customs have to adapt to the new law by September 1.
DIENA

- Opposition parties say parliament speaker Alfreds Chepanis may have exceeded his powers when consenting to extend an agreement between German Kienast Metall and the Russian ministry of defence on econstruction works in Liepaja port.
- The U.S. Congress accepted a draft law calling for the Baltic states and Romania to be admitted to NATO and to be supported financially in meeting NATO standards.
- A new non-governmental organisation, the European Movement in Latvia, has been formed to promote discussion in Latvia about EU issues and to promote favourable attitude to the EU.
- Parliament passed amendments in a package of laws to protect witnesses and victims of crime.
- Opposition MPs introduced a draft resolution for a no-confidence vote aainst Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans for possible violations of the anti-corruption law.
- The budget surplus on June 6 was 10.15 million lats.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE
- The prosecutors office appealed against the verdict of Riga district court to discharge Ivan Haritonov, an allegede leader of orgainised crime.
BIZNES & BALTIYA
- Air Baltic and SAS signed an agreement with the Latvian national opera on further co-operation.

- The head of the state revenue service Andrejs Sonchiks said the finance police have evidence showing a breach of anti-corruption laws by 27 high-ranking officials. Under the law, officials cannot hold private and public posts.
DIENAS BIZNESS
- The Latvian Investment Bank, in co-operation with Estonian leasing company Estonian Industrial Leasing, has established a Latvian Industrial Leasing company.
- The total number of passengers in January-May 1997 having used Riga international airport grew an average five percent to 189,898 people.
